title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Java locals, honest caches, a Run button that runs
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.10 closes the fifth audit: a dead-code corpus that a cancelled scan could poison, Java parameters that Rename treated as workspace symbols, an Android Run button that could pin a non-existent Gradle task forever, and a Logcat banner whose trigger could never fire.

highlights.title: A cancelled scan cannot poison Remove All
highlights.description: A dead-code scan cut short by Cancel left no trace of the files it skipped, was cached for a minute, and "Remove All Unreferenced Symbols" could delete code those files use. Cancelled scans are never cached, and saving a source invalidates the corpus.

highlights.title: Java parameters are locals
highlights.description: The scope index only knew Kotlin's fun. In a Java method, Cmd+Click on a parameter jumped to a Kotlin property elsewhere and F2 renamed every same-named symbol the workspace could reach. Parameters, locals and lambda parameters resolve inside the method now.

highlights.title: Android Run that recovers
highlights.description: A discovery timeout no longer pins a non-existent install task forever, the Run button gets its command back once the project resolves, the launch uses the resolved adb binary, and the Logcat "adb not found" banner finally has a trigger that fires.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fetches AndroidX and Google library sources from Google's Maven, counts progress once per coordinate, and reports failures in a message.
Reads the library sources bar right (missing/total, real stdlib state, live reaction to kotlinJump.indexSourcesJars) and fixes plurals and empty summaries in the dead-code commands.
